Constellation to send SOC2 attestation PDF and SSO/SAML metadata by 2026-11-12
Schedule staging demo of private deployment reference architecture with Liam for week of 2026-11-16

Liam O'Connor: Provide SSO metadata, KMS requirements, and internal network diagram (due 2026-11-12)

Packaging options: hosted API vs dedicated vs private deploy
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Ravi Patel (Redwood); Aisha Khan, Tom Reeves, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Martinez (Constellation)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick roll call. Maya from Redwood here, i think we have Diego and Ravi, and on the Constellation side?
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Hey it's Aisha, hi all. Tom's here, Liam and Sofia as well. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Awesome. Goal for today is to align on the marketplace listing requirements and the reference architecture for the joint solution so we can scope the staging demo and the listing publish process. Roughly 45 minutes.
[00:28] Diego Alvarez: I'll jump into the techs, mainly VPC/private deploy options, terraform snippets, KMS and SSO.
[00:34] Tom Reeves: High level from marketplace PM side, I'm primarily interested in listing metadata, icons, pricing tier fields, and any technical prerequisites we need to show in the listing.
[00:45] Maya Chen: Great. Quick background: Redwood supports hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For marketplace we'd typically surface the hosted integration for self-serve, but we also provide a reference architecture for private deployments if a customer is enterprise and wants a VPC or on-prem offering.
[01:10] Liam O'Connor: For Constellation some key constraints: we need SSO/SAML integration for marketplace launch, KMS backend for keys, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also, any certs for data at rest are important because of customer requirements.
[01:28] Sofia Martinez: Right, SOC 2 and ISO references are a must, and we need to confirm where the logs live and retention windows.
[01:36] Ravi Patel: On the Redwood side we can provide SOC2 attestation doc, audit log samples, and options for KMS where the customer can either use Redwood-managed KMS or integrate their own KMS via a HSM/KMS connector in the private deployment. For marketplace listing we usually link to the compliance pack.
[01:58] Aisha Khan: For the marketplace listing process, are there special network requirements we need to call out? Some of our partners need explicit IP allowlists or VPC peering details.
[02:10] Diego Alvarez: Good question. For hosted API we don't require VPC peering, but if you want private deployment or dedicated, we'll produce a reference arch that includes VPC peering options, ingress/egress rules, and terraform modules. For marketplace we can put a small note: "Private deployment available - contact sales for VPC peering details".
[02:30] Tom Reeves: Also need to know billing flow. Does Redwood expect to bill the end customer directly if listed on Constellation's marketplace, or do we do a reseller/commission flow?
[02:42] Maya Chen: That depends on the marketplace integration model. We support both direct billing and marketplace-mediated billing; we'll need to confirm Constellation's preferred flow and the contract model. We can add pricing fields to the listing and specify whether meter/bill is via Constellation or Redwood.
[02:58] Tom Reeves: Okay please send the pricing spreadsheet; we need columns for per-token pricing, per-embedding price, and committed capacity options.
[03:08] Maya Chen: Will do. I'll include recommended starter tiers.
[03:12] [03:15] Diego Alvarez: Back to the reference architecture - typical pattern: control plane in Redwood-managed account (for hosted and marketplace metadata), with runtime either in Redwood cloud for hosted/Dedicated or customer VPC for private. For private we have a small agent/connector plus terraform for provisioning, and an optional KMS integration for key control.
[03:40] Liam O'Connor: For the private option, what's the network egress model? We have strict requirements for egress only to designated endpoints.
[03:48] Diego Alvarez: We can lock egress down to Redwood's runtime endpoints and provide a list of CIDR ranges; in private deploy we can host runtime inside your VPC so egress is internal. We'll provide a runbook and network ACL templates.
[04:05] Sofia Martinez: On KMS - can you support a customer-managed AWS KMS key and rotate keys on our schedule?
[04:12] Ravi Patel: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for the private deployment. For hosted API you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via an integration; we'll document the handshake for granting Redwood the ability to use the key while retaining control. Rotation schedule is configurable.
[04:28] Aisha Khan: Any blockers from Redwood to be listed in our marketplace? There are a few mandatory metadata fields: logo 1024x1024, short description, compliance badges, support URL, and a tech contact.
[04:41] Maya Chen: We can supply assets and metadata. We'll get logo, short/long descriptions, screenshots, and links to support docs. For tech contact use diego@redwood.ai and maya@redwood.ai.
[04:53] Tom Reeves: Also need a short video or quick demo clip. Can you provide a 1-2 minute clip of the hosted flow?
[05:00] Diego Alvarez: Yep, we have a <120s demo clip. We'll drop a link in the asset packet.
[05:05] [05:12] Liam O'Connor: On the integration side, can you share terraform snippets or helm charts for the reference arch? We want to include those as a GitHub repo linked from the listing.
[05:21] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely. I'll prepare a repo with terraform modules for VPC, subnets, security groups, and a small agent install chart. We'll also include example outputs for KMS and SSO SAML metadata.
[05:35] Maya Chen: One ask from our legal team is to confirm data residency for EU customers; can Constellation indicate whether the marketplace will surface region-specific offerings?
[05:44] Tom Reeves: Yes, we'll support region flags on the listing, and we can mark EU-only offerings. We need the region-specific performance profiles and costs.
[05:53] Ravi Patel: We'll share a short matrix mapping model variants (quantized, fp16, etc.) to latency characteristics by region so you can show expected latency/cost on the listing.
[06:05] Sofia Martinez: On audit logging, what format do logs take? JSON lines, syslog? We need SIEM ingestion examples.
[06:13] Diego Alvarez: Audit logs are JSON lines with standard fields (timestamp, request_id, user_id, action, tokens_consumed). We can provide a sample stream and an ingestion guide.
[06:25] Aisha Khan: Great. On timeline - what's realistic for a staged demo -> listing publish?
[06:32] Maya Chen: If we get the SOC2 and SSO metadata quickly and Redwood provides assets and terraform repo, we can do a staging demo in 1-2 weeks and aim for listing publish ~3-4 weeks, pending legal/billing integration.
[06:46] Tom Reeves: That timeline works if we get the artifact packet by next week.
[06:51] Maya Chen: We'll aim to send the packet by 2026-11-10.
[06:55] [07:00] Diego Alvarez: A few technical caveats: for private deployments we recommend a minimum of 2 GPU nodes for the runtime to meet availability; also KV cache placement matters for latency - if you're serving US customers, place KV cache in US region. I'll include sizing guidance.
[07:18] Liam O'Connor: Good to know. For the staging demo, can we provision a small private environment in our dev VPC? We can give you temporary credentials.
[07:26] Ravi Patel: Yes, that's ideal. We'll run the agent in your dev VPC and we'll walk through the install. Diego will own the runbook.
[07:34] Sofia Martinez: Regarding RBAC, we need to map Constellation roles to Redwood roles for support-level access. Is there an SCIM/SSO mapping?
[07:43] Diego Alvarez: We support SAML-based role mapping and SCIM for user provisioning. We'll provide attribute mapping examples (email -> principal, groups -> roles).
[07:53] Aisha Khan: Competitors: a couple of our partners asked to compare to CloudMart and Aurora - any quick differentiators?
[07:59] Maya Chen: Redwood focuses on production-grade inference controls, explicit batching and caching knobs, and a unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, which simplifies ops. We can share a short comparison doc.
[08:12] Tom Reeves: Perfect. Any security paperwork or templates you can share for the marketplace security review?
[08:18] Ravi Patel: We'll toss you the security pack: SOC2 report, encryption at rest/in transit docs, penetration test summary (redacted), and our incident response contact.
[08:28] Maya Chen: I'll attach that to the asset packet.
[08:32] [08:40] Diego Alvarez: Quick note on the listing metadata: include a field for "Deployment Options" where you can select hosted, dedicated, private; we'll supply recommended default copy for each. Also include a checkbox for "Requires SSO" if private deploy is precondition.
[08:56] Tom Reeves: We'll add those fields. Anything else from Constellation side?
[09:02] Aisha Khan: We'll validate legal flow - whether we take commissions or enable direct billing. I'll sync with finance and get back by 2026-11-09.
[09:12] Maya Chen: Great. Recap of action items and next steps - we'll send listing assets and pricing, Diego will create terraform repo and runbook, Constellation to send SSO and SOC docs. Schedule staging demo week of 11/16.
[09:28] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Quick question: can we run a short benchmark (latency/cost) against a small prompt set during staging to validate performance claims?
[09:36] Ravi Patel: Yes, we'll coordinate a bench run. Please share the prompt set; we'll run it and provide token counts and p95 latency numbers.
[09:46] Tom Reeves: I'll prepare a short prompt pack.
[09:49] Maya Chen: Cool. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in an email with the packet and calendar invites.
[09:56] Aisha Khan: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:00] End of recording.
